clue.text: Environmentalist identifies the knack of growing plants

parts.note: a Green is a campaigner for the environment
to finger someone is to identify them, as a witness might

explanation.surface: An eco-campaigner is credited with knowing how to make plants thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'identifies' does double duty in the surface but in the wordplay it is the verb 'fingers', naming a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a natural talent for gardening, the British counterpart of the American 'green thumb'.

clue.text: Arise and get something to grow tomatoes in

parts.note: to grow is to arise or develop
to bag something is to get or secure it

explanation.surface: An instruction to get up and fetch a container for the tomato crop.
explanation.walkthrough: A growbag is a British gardening staple: a plastic sack of compost laid flat for planting directly into.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners commonly plant tomatoes straight into these compost-filled plastic sacks on patios and in greenhouses.

clue.text: Blow up corrupt general

indicators.note: something corrupt has been twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A call to bomb a crooked military commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' reads as an explosion but here means to make bigger, as with a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make a bigger print of it, so the phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Blair's party is unfamiliar with the workers

parts.note: something new is not yet familiar
labour is the workforce collectively

explanation.surface: A jibe that Tony Blair's party has lost touch with working people.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair rebranded the British Labour Party under this name when he led it in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the rebranded name of the British centre-left party that Tony Blair led to power in 1997.

clue.text: Ron is about to produce golf clubs

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word is wraps the name Ron

parts.note: taken as written; this is the outer part
taken as written; this goes inside

explanation.surface: Ron is on the point of bringing out his golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' is the wrapping instruction and 'to produce' joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers carry a set of metal-headed clubs numbered for different distances, collectively known by this name.

clue.text: Old king's secret? He smiles a lot!

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
inner thoughts are private, kept secret

explanation.surface: A royal mystery: what is the old monarch's secret? He is always cheerful!
explanation.walkthrough: GR, Georgius Rex, appears on British post boxes from the reigns of the King Georges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who constantly beams with a broad smile can be described informally as a cheerful smiler of this kind.

clue.text: Cook one a brown trout

indicators.note: to cook is to mix and transform ingredients, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe step: cook a single brown trout.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs brown with trout, and brown trout is a real species, which hides that the definition is a different trout.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow is a common species of trout, so the clue defines by giving the broader category.

clue.text: Theory of knowledge is — gee! — simply too complicated!

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so these letters need untangling into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated student complains that the philosophy of knowledge is just too hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is the link, not part of the fodder: the twelve letters come from gee, simply and too.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of philosophy studies the nature, sources and limits of what people can know.

clue.text: Lowly canon's measure to help the needy

parts.note: poor means humble or lowly
a canon is a rule or law

explanation.surface: A humble churchman's scheme for helping the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canon' suggests a clergyman, but here it is a rule. The Poor Law was England's historic system of relief for paupers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Poor Laws were English statutes establishing parish relief and workhouses for destitute people.

clue.text: View duck taking wing

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the zero-shaped letter
a pinion is the outer part of a bird's wing

explanation.surface: Watching a duck take to the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking wing' reads as flying off; in fact 'taking' simply joins the zero to the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A view in the sense of a belief or judgement someone holds is a synonym.

clue.text: Cuckoo, wren, tern — shot going towards the Manchester area?

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the following bird names are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of birds, one apparently shot down, heading for Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuckoo looks like a fourth bird in the list, but it is the scrambling signal; shot is fodder, not a second signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester lies in England's north-west, so travelling there from the south means heading in that compass direction.

clue.text: Part of Russia, southern Spain and Portugal

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
the Iberian peninsula holds these two countries

explanation.surface: A geography list of places: a Russian region, plus southern Spain and Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast Asian territory east of the Urals forms the largest region of the Russian Federation.

clue.text: Smooth lawyers for offshore bank

parts.note: to sand is to smooth with sandpaper
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: Slick legal advisers for a tax-haven bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offshore bank' suggests tax havens; it is a ridge of sand in shallow water.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of sediment built up by currents in shallow water off a coast is a literal bank lying offshore.

clue.text: Bird dog, losing its head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and losing it drops that letter

parts.note: a beagle is a small hound

explanation.surface: A bird dog, the kind used in hunting, has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird dog' reads as one phrase, a gundog, but Bird is the definition and dog the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The large raptor is a familiar example of a bird, so the definition is the general category.

clue.text: Shoot is blooming and burgeoning

parts.note: a flower that is blooming is out
burgeoning is growth, the noun sense

explanation.surface: A plant shoot is flowering and sprouting vigorously.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is about plants, so blooming and burgeoning look like descriptions, not the two halves of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot is new stem or branch springing from a plant, something that grows out from it.

clue.text: Pilot and chauffeur try out new car

parts.note: a pilot study is a test
to chauffeur someone is to drive them

explanation.surface: An aviator and a professional driver take a new car out for a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: Pilot and chauffeur read as two people, but each is a verb or modifier giving a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Before buying, motorists take a vehicle on the road briefly to judge how it handles.

clue.text: Approaches unhappy voter with dubious ruse

indicators.note: unhappy suggests something out of sorts, so the word that follows is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dubious means not straight, so the word that follows is bent into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A canvasser woos a disgruntled voter with a shady trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word is rearranged on its own, and the two results simply join.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtures are tentative approaches made to open negotiations or a relationship.

clue.text: Fugitive in disguise reaches Cape Endeavour

indicators.note: something in disguise is concealed, so the word lies hidden inside the clue's letters

parts.note: the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: A runaway in disguise makes it to a remote cape.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Endeavour sounds like a real headland; the answer runs across the end of reaches, all of Cape and the start of Endeavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has broken out of custody and is on the run is a fugitive.

clue.text: Doctor, artisan and old empress

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of people: a physician, a craftsman and an elderly empress.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a noun in a list of people but is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: The title was held by the wife of a Russian tsar or a woman ruling Russia before 1917.

clue.text: Effluent from Iowa steelworks

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters are lifted out of the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of Iowa and the start of steelworks

explanation.surface: Pollution discharged by a steel plant in Iowa.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluent is liquid discharge, sewage or industrial outflow, that must be disposed of.

clue.text: Picture composed of trees and a waterway

parts.note: a wood is a group of trees
a cut is a British term for a canal

explanation.surface: A landscape painting of woodland and a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a canal is often called a cut, since it was dug out by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A print made from a carved block of timber is a kind of picture.

clue.text: Paul's so wrong regarding marriage

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so these letters need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Paul has got it badly wrong about wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to a husband or wife and the married relationship.

clue.text: Land planted with fruit trees or beet

parts.note: taken as written
chard is a leafy variety of beet

explanation.surface: A choice of crops for a plot: fruit trees or beetroot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs almost to the end, so only the last two words supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the ordinary word for a plot cultivated with apple, pear or other fruit-bearing trees.

clue.text: Figure? Mine has sex appeal!

parts.note: to mine is to dig
it is an old slang term for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their figure is attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as a possessive, but it is the verb meaning excavate.
explanation.definitionFit: A single numeral from zero to nine is also called a figure.

clue.text: Doctor attends operation; on strike, he refuses to participate further

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
op is short for operation
striking workers are out

explanation.surface: A surgeon at an operation goes on strike and refuses to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: The striking doctor seems to be the subject, but the definition is only the final clause, about someone who quits.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who abandons a course, or society's conventions, withdraws and will not take part any more.

clue.text: Gay turned round very quietly in Barking

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the flipped word goes around what follows
turned means flipped about, so the word gay is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheerful dog has gone soft and quiet in the middle of barking.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the place in east London; it is the definition, a dog's noise. pp is the musical marking pianissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: Yapping is the shrill repeated noise a small dog makes, a kind of barking.

clue.text: One starts to notice Cherokee Indian with singular gold tooth

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first letter of each of these three words
s is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Someone begins to spot a Native American with a single gold tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: Or is gold in heraldry, from the French.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the sharp front biting teeth, so it names a particular tooth.

clue.text: Lunatic prattled name of French region

definitions.note: adjective: relating to a French administrative district

indicators.note: lunatic means mad, so the words that follow are wildly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A madman babbled the name of a region of France.
explanation.walkthrough: France is divided into administrative areas called départements, so the adjective can mean relating to one.
explanation.definitionFit: France's local administrative units are départements, and the adjective describes anything belonging to such a unit.
